sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH

items.q: Match the following multifactorial target — 1) Blood pressure 2) LDL cholesterol 3) Aspirin 4) Proteinuria … A) <130/80 mmHg (<120/80 with CKD) B) <130 (or <100, <70, <55 by risk) C) 75 mg >40 yr with one risk factor D) ACEi + SGLT2i + finerenone
items.exp: BP target <130/80 (<120/80 with CKD); LDL targets vary by risk (130/100/70/55); aspirin 75 mg >40 yr with risk factors; proteinuria uses ACEi + SGLT2i + finerenone. (Book p935)

items.q: A 60-year-old with T2DM and established CVD has LDL 130 mg/dL. The most appropriate lipid management is:
items.exp: Established CVD with LDL 130 mg/dL warrants high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg). (Book p935)

items.q: Assess BP targets: I <130/80 mmHg is the general diabetes target. II <120/80 mmHg is preferred in CKD with proteinuria.
items.exp: <130/80 mmHg is the standard target; <120/80 mmHg is preferred in CKD with proteinuria, per page and KDIGO guidance. (Book p935)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a first-line antihypertensive in T2DM?
items.exp: Amlodipine monotherapy is not preferred; ACEi/ARB is first-line, with CCB combined. The page mentions cilnidipine / benidipine as CCB options in combination. (Book p935)

items.q: In T2DM with albuminuria, the triple combination for renal protection includes ACEi, SGLT2i and ___.
items.exp: Finerenone is the non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist added on top of ACEi and SGLT2i for diabetic kidney disease. (Book p935)

items.q: Match the following agent to its lipid-lowering effect — 1) Atorvastatin 2) Rosuvastatin 3) Ezetimibe 4) PCSK9 inhibitor … A) High-intensity statin 40–80 mg B) High-intensity statin 20–40 mg C) NPC1L1 inhibitor, add-on D) LDL-R upregulator, injectable
items.exp: Atorvastatin 40–80 mg and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg are high-intensity statins; ezetimibe blocks NPC1L1; PCSK9 inhibitors upregulate LDL receptor. (Book p935)

items.q: A 55-year-old with T2DM on high-intensity statin has LDL 95 mg/dL and a recent MI. The most appropriate add-on is:
opts: Ezetimibe first, then PCSK9 inhibitor if needed
items.exp: After high-intensity statin, ezetimibe is added first; PCSK9 inhibitors are used for further LDL reduction in very high-risk patients. (Book p935)

items.q: Assess NASH: I Semaglutide and saroglitazar improve NASH. II Pioglitazone is contraindicated in NASH with HF.
items.exp: Semaglutide and saroglitazar improve NASH; pioglitazone also improves NASH but is contraindicated in HF. (Book p935)

items.q: Match the following scenario to the LDL target — 1) >40 yr no other risk 2) One additional ASCVD risk factor 3) High-risk (CKD, severe AS) 4) Established CVD … A) <130 mg/dL B) <100 mg/dL C) <70 mg/dL D) <55 mg/dL
items.exp: The page lists stepwise LDL targets: <130, <100, <70 and <55 mg/dL depending on risk; established CVD is the strictest (<55 mg/dL). (Book p935)

items.q: A 70-year-old with T2DM, CKD and proteinuria has BP 142/86 mmHg. The most appropriate antihypertensive strategy is:
opts: ACEi or ARB + CCB (cilnidipine / benidipine) with SGLT2i
items.exp: ACEi/ARB is first-line for diabetic kidney disease; CCB combination achieves BP targets; SGLT2i provides additional renal protection. (Book p935)

items.q: Aspirin 75 mg daily is recommended in diabetes patients over ___ years with at least one additional ASCVD risk factor.
items.exp: Aspirin 75 mg daily is recommended in patients >40 yr with at least one additional ASCVD risk factor (not in low-risk patients due to bleeding). (Book p935)

items.q: Assess multifactorial care: I Lifestyle intervention remains the foundation. II Multifactorial care reduces long-term complications.
items.exp: Lifestyle intervention is the foundation; multifactorial care reduces both micro- and macrovascular complications long-term. (Book p935)
